item.text: {"question_id":"2B.7","answer":"During the 2023 period, López Obrador’s government participated in and supported peace processes: Mexico served as a guarantor in Colombia’s dialogue with the ELN, hosted Venezuela negotiations facilitated by Norway, supported implementation of the November 2022 Mexico City agreements, and kept channels open for their resumption (BATCH-0048-E014). Mexico also proposed a UN-linked Russia–Ukraine caucus to promote confidence-building and mediation, but the supplied record documents advocacy and consultations—not formation of the caucus, a ceasefire, a signed settlement, or a verified durable outcome (BATCH-0045-E012). The record therefore supports concrete diplomatic engagement and support for existing processes, but not a finding that López Obrador negotiated, implemented, complied with, or made a major international agreement durable. His condemnation of Russia’s invasion and continued neutrality, including refusal to sanction Moscow, provide mixed context but do not establish ceasefire performance (BATCH-0048-E014; BATCH-0042-E007). North American cooperation continued in 2023 despite disputes, but this is not evidence of a peace agreement or confidence-building measure within the question’s narrow sense (BATCH-0051-E020).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0045-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E007","BATCH-0051-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not independently verify implementation, compliance, monitoring, or durability of the Colombian or Venezuelan processes.","No supplied item documents a López Obrador-era signed ceasefire, peace treaty, lawful settlement, or verified outcome led or made durable by his government.","The strongest evidence for the Russia–Ukraine initiative is an official statement of advocacy and intended consultations, not evidence of execution or effect.","Domestic militarization and criminal violence are excluded because they do not establish failure to uphold an applicable international ceasefire or settlement."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed domestic militarization and criminal-violence evidence as irrelevant to this international ceasefire-and-settlement question.","Reduced positive weight assigned to declaratory diplomacy and distinguished advocacy from negotiation, implementation, compliance, and durable outcomes.","Retained the material evidence of Mexico’s guarantor role, hosting of Venezuelan negotiations, and stated support for implementing the November 2022 agreements.","Preserved uncertainty about independent verification, causal effect, and durability."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if independent UN, Norway, Colombian, Venezuelan, or other monitoring records establish Mexico’s concrete actions, compliance, or measurable effects in these peace processes.","Reopen if evidence shows whether the November 2022 Venezuelan agreements were implemented, suspended, resumed, or made durable during the target period."]}
